sowhat.text: Large strategic deals keep getting signed, from CrowdStrike's all-stock Zscaler bid to Sanofi's cash offer for Insmed, and the Lukoil sale shows energy M&A running through sanctions approvals. With the 10-year at 4.94%, debt-funded buyers face a high base rate, which favors stock deals and strategics.

pitch: Stocks ended a big week on a high note. In the shortened Black Friday session the S&P 500 rose 1.6% to about 7,300, led by chips, and gained about 5.6% on the week. Rates moved the other way: the 10-year climbed to about 4.94% and the Fed sits at 3.75 to 4% with a meeting on 8 and 9 December, after the jobs report on the 4th. Oil is firm, with Brent near $95 and WTI near $83 on supply fears in the Gulf. On deals, CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler for about $44 billion in stock and Sanofi is buying Insmed for $41 billion in cash, so big strategic deals are getting done even with rates this high.

quiz.q: Where did the 10-year Treasury yield end on Fri 27 Nov?
What drove the S&P 500's 1.6% gain on Fri 27 Nov?
quiz.a: A rebound in chip stocks, which lifted technology and every S&P sector fund.

quiz.q: Who is acquiring Zscaler, and how is the roughly $43.9B deal paid for?
quiz.a: CrowdStrike, in an all-stock deal at 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per Zscaler share.

chat.q: What's your read on rates right now?
chat.a: The 10-year ended at 4.94%, up 9 bp from Wednesday, with the 2-year at 4.69%. The Fed funds range is 3.75–4.00% after a hike in September, and the jobs report on 4 Dec comes right before the 8-9 Dec FOMC. For deals, a high base rate makes leveraged buyouts harder to finance and favors strategics paying in stock or cash.
chat.tip: Lead with the 10-year, then tie it to financing.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: Brent settled at $95.44 and WTI at $83.08, a spread of about $12. Reports pointed to attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and on Saudi infrastructure, and OPEC+ meets Sunday. Firm crude supports upstream cash flow and energy deal appetite, but adds to inflation pressure.
chat.tip: Name both benchmarks and the spread.

chat.a: CrowdStrike is buying Zscaler for about $43.9B in stock, advised by Qatalyst, J.P. Morgan and BofA for CrowdStrike and BDT & MSD, Citi and Goldman for Zscaler. Sanofi is buying Insmed for about $41.0B in cash. Both show large strategic deals proceeding despite a 4.94% 10-year.

chat.q: Why did stocks jump on Black Friday?
chat.a: The S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,297 and the Nasdaq 2.3%, led by chip stocks rebounding after the prior week's AI selling. The week was the S&P's best, up 5.6%. The VIX closed at 23.81. A calmer tape helps IPO and financing windows reopen, though volumes were thin in a half-day.
chat.tip: Mention the thin holiday volume to show judgment.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: A higher risk-free rate raises the discount rate, so present value falls, most for long-duration cash flows and terminal value. From today's 4.94% that would mean about 5.44%. Highly levered buyers would also see financing costs rise, pressuring LBO returns.
chat.tip: Walk through the WACC mechanics first.

chat.q: Walk me through how an all-stock deal like CrowdStrike and Zscaler works.
chat.a: Each Zscaler share converts to 1.135 CrowdStrike shares, valuing Zscaler at about $43.9B enterprise value, a roughly 34% premium. CrowdStrike holders would own about 84.1% of the combined company. All-stock avoids new debt at a 4.94% 10-year, but exposes both sides to CrowdStrike's share price until closing.
chat.tip: Cover premium, exchange ratio and ownership split.

chat.q: Why might energy M&A run through sanctions approvals, as in the Lukoil sale?
chat.a: The Eldridge-led consortium would swap restricted Russian shares for 100% of LUKOIL International, which has about 350,000 boe/d of upstream output and three refineries. It needs conditional OFAC approval, so regulatory structure matters as much as price. With Brent at $95.44, the assets are valuable, but closing certainty drives the timeline.
chat.tip: Frame it as deal certainty versus valuation.
